enAudit: G1-264 undercounts: the title "When Two Words Start the Same" and the instruction "Two words start alike" describe two words, but the render carries SIX words in TWO same-initial pairs (baby/boat, scooter/swing). Should read "some words start with the same letter" or "two pairs".

G2-281 (RESOLVED by the coordinator: names removed, ends now . or ?, three lanes). Two residual notes. (1) The old spec file types/g2/G2-281-fix-the-sentence-capital-and-full-stop.js is STILL ON DISK beside the new G2-281-fix-the-sentence-capital-and-end-mark.js — two files declaring id G2-281. loadType currently resolves to the new one, but that is filename-order luck, not a guarantee; delete the stale file. (2) out/b2var-sweep/g2281-animals.png was regenerated at 20:39 with only the names half of the fix: it still renders FOUR lanes, the old title and a full-stop-only instruction, so it no longer shows the shipping face.

G1-283 instruction claims "Find the one order that works", which is false for card 4: "giraffe / is / your / this" yields both "Is this your giraffe?" and "This is your giraffe." Two grammatical orders, so the uniqueness claim is wrong on that card. (Cards 1 and 3 also contain the names emma and ben, which the child must capitalise even though the page says there are no capitals.)

G2-293 repeats a problem: card 1 ("Mia pays for [red fish 40] with 25+25") and card 3 ("Mia buys [red fish 40] and pays with 25+25") are the same child, the same item, the same coins and the same answer, on a page of only three cards.

G1-282 instruction is now half-true after its fix: "The capital letter and the end mark show where each sentence begins." The capital shows where it begins; the END MARK shows where it ENDS. The pre-fix text said "starts and ends" and the fix dropped the half the end mark actually signals.

out/b2var-faces.json theme field is wrong for three rows and contradicts the shipping wave: G1-283 says vehicles (wave = animals), G3-372 says vehicles (wave = fruits), G3-376 says vehicles (wave = toys). All three are the same stale value. Worse, G1-283 sweep path out/b2var-sweep/g1283-vehicles.png DOES NOT EXIST on disk (the render is g1283-animals.png), and g3372/g3376-vehicles.png show a theme that will not ship. A panel that trusts this field names the wrong pictures, and the theme also feeds the SEO description lead.

The grouping-division stories state the arrangement as already done while the picture deliberately shows the objects UNGROUPED: G3-374 card 2 "Tom arranges 10 cranberries in rows of 5" is drawn as one row of 10; G3-375 card 2 "Lily arranges 20 koalas in rows of 5" is drawn as two rows of 10; G3-376 card 2 "Ben lines up 30 cranes in 6 equal rows" is drawn as two rows of 15; G3-373 card 1 "There are 10 airplanes. Ben makes groups of 5" is the only one phrased correctly. The child is meant to MAKE the groups, so the completed-action wording contradicts the render. Use "wants to arrange … in rows of 5".

K-296 instruction drops "Start at the orange dot", which both of its siblings (K-294, K-295) carry and which the page needs: the render has the orange start dot at 11 and the child must know where to begin. Its title also wraps to two lines at the rendered width.

G2-298 (Days of the Week) places two picture stickers on the calendar (the 16th and the 28th) that no question refers to, on a page whose instruction says every question is about the days of the week. The sibling G2-296 does ask about its sticker; here they are pure noise for a 7-year-old.

G2-287 uses the bare word chip "crane" with no picture. MEMORY records crane as already mistranslated to the BIRD in es/no/da/sv/fi; with no picture to disambiguate, those locales will ship the wrong sense in a vehicles-themed page. (nl kraan is safe either way.)

out/b2var-faces.json enTitle/enInstruction are STALE against the renders for at least K-289, K-291, K-298, G1-263, G1-278, G1-282 and G2-285: the nine already-fixed defects were fixed in the generator but never back-ported to the face table. K-298 is still listed there as "Copy the Picture on a 6x6 Grid" (titled by size, the defect that was fixed) while the page itself reads "Copy the Grid Picture: First Steps". Since the brief tells panels the face table is authoritative, every future panel inherits the pre-fix English unless it opens the PNGs.

nl sentence-bank note supporting the G2-281 redesign: of the 15 nl frames marked uses:[fix], 6 are name-free and only TWO of those end in a full stop (De {noun} zijn heel groot./klein.) against FOUR ending in a question mark. On a three-lane name-free page a Dutch child is therefore guaranteed at least one question, and usually two or three, so any nl copy naming only de punt would be false on most draws.

G1-297 EN instruction "Bigger groups to halve, starting from twenty" is wrong at both ends: hMin 5 / hMax 10 prints groups of 2m, i.e. 10 to 20, so twenty is the CEILING, not the start. Its twin G1-296 gets the same parameter right ("all the way to twenty").

G1-289 EN instruction "The top brick is given and the bottom row is not" is false. topGiven clears every brick, restores the apex, and then restores ONE brick per course down to r=0 — so exactly one bottom-row brick is always printed. A child told the bottom row is blank is looking for a wall that is not on the page.

G1-286 EN instruction "Count the bigger groups, double them, and halve them" reads as if each group gets both operations; the render gives each card ONE pill, either double or half. The shipped nl base (G1-247) already says it correctly — "verdubbel de ENE groep en halveer de ANDERE" — so the English is the weaker of the two.

K-308 / G1-285 / G2-304 EN instructions all assert "Ten numbered dots". That ten is the INHERITED d1 window, not a parameter these faces pin, so it is exactly the count the brief warns will stale on a retune. It also collides with the real dot count, which stays 20 — "ten numbered dots to join backwards" reads as a ten-dot picture. G2-314 has the mirror problem: its instruction says "to 100", which is only true because window:10 is inherited, while its own title ("Count by Tens") declines to claim it.

G2-312 EN title "How Many Days Later?" and instruction "Use the calendar to work out each date" fit only half the page. Of the four questions, `after` answers a COUNT of days and `dayOfDate` answers a WEEKDAY NAME; neither is a date. (The Dutch week correctly starts on maandag — CALENDAR.nl.weekStart is 1 — so that earlier finding is closed.)

G2-313 EN instruction "Each brick is the sum of the two under it" is the GENRE sentence, not this face: it is what the base G1-246 already says, and it mentions none of what makes G2-313 different (four courses, base given, totals reaching 100). Same class as G1-300, whose "Sort each word into the right bin" names neither of its two bins nor the fact that this is the only word-classes face with no pictures at all.

K-313 EN instruction "This time the word for many is given. Write the word for just one" leaves out the scaffold that separates it from K-316: at K-313 plurModel is NOT false, so the singular is still printed as a DASHED model the child traces first. As written, the English for K-313 and K-316 asks for the same thing on two deliberately different pages.

G2-307 and G2-311 are titled "Fix the Sentence: Where Does It End?" and "Where Does It End?" — near-duplicates that also drop the family head from the second one, while the parameter that actually separates them (ends ['.'] with needCaps 1 versus ends ['.','?'] with needQ 1) appears in neither title.

G1-301 / G1-303 / G1-304 EN instructions name the letter boxes but not the writing line. In G1-244 the `right` ruling is built on EVERY card regardless of `boxes`, so these three faces carry TWO writing surfaces — a ruled line beside the picture and a row of boxes beneath it — and the English mentions only one of them. A 6-year-old told to write one letter per box has an unexplained ruled line to account for.

K-311 / K-315 are the one place the brief's rule 5 cannot hold: traceLane:false leaves a caption model and two EMPTY rails, so nothing on the page is traced and the family head ("Trace and Write the Words" / nl "Woorden overtrekken") would be a false title. We changed the verb in nl — overtrekken becomes overschrijven — and kept the noun. Recommend the English do the same rather than dropping the family word entirely as "Copy the Word" does.

K-309 latent contract mismatch (nl unaffected, but it will bite): the alphabet path takes its sequence from COLLATION[loc].strip, while verify() proves ordering with localeCompare(). Those agree only where the printed strip happens to match Unicode collation. nl is plain a-z so it is safe, but a locale whose strip carries an appended letter would fail verify on a correct page.
